exposure: Maternal race/ethnicity (American Indian/Alaska Native vs. White)
cohort: The study included all live births to individuals identified as American Indian, Alaska Native, or White, residing in the 50 US states or the District of Columbia in 2017.
finding: After adjusting for differences in cesarean indication, age, and clinical and obstetric risk factors, the cesarean birth incidence among American Indian and Alaska Natives was 3.2 percentage points higher than among White individuals.
mod_finding: Cesarean birth incidence remained higher and increased in magnitude among American Indian and Alaska Natives in Robson groups 1 (low risk, primary), 6 (nulliparous, breech presentation), and 9 (transverse/oblique lie) after adjustment.
